title: MP Materials' 10X Financing: Cash, Covenants, and Construction Risk

publication_cover.title:
MP Materials'
10X Financing
publication_cover.subtitle: Cash, Covenants, and Construction Risk
publication_cover.dek: How a JPMorgan–Goldman Sachs commitment of at least $1bn gave way to $724.2m of net equity and a $275m JPMorgan-agented revolver, and what that means for funding 10X before it earns revenue.
publication_cover.context: 10X is MP's planned rare-earth magnet plant in Northlake, Texas. MP expects to invest more than $1.25bn; construction is underway and commissioning is expected in 2028.
publication_cover.attribution: Independent research; not commissioned or reviewed by JPMorgan or MP Materials. Held from publication pending human review.

exhibit.subtitle: USD million at three reported dates; no loans were drawn at any of them
exhibit.annotation: Letters of credit are the revolver's only reported use. The $203m can be drawn only while the agreement's conditions are met, so it supports liquidity without counting as cash. Letters of credit and loans share the $275m commitment.

exhibit.title: Liquid assets fell $492.4m in nine months, mostly from $420.3m of capital spending and $91.1m of financing outflows
exhibit.subtitle: Reported USD million, 31 December 2025 to 30 September 2026
exhibit.annotation: Capital spending covers every company project, of which 10X is one; MP guides to $500m to $600m of 2026 capital costs net of government awards. The $7.8m operating outflow includes $110.9m of price-protection receipts.

exhibit.title: An actual suspension of a Defense payment obligation blocks revolver draws at once; lenders may act after 60 or 90 days
exhibit.subtitle: Revolver states under credit agreement Section 8.01(m); the revolver was available at 30 September 2026
exhibit.annotation: Plain reading of the filed credit agreement; not legal advice. The clock starts when an obligation is actually suspended or released; whether a right to suspend already counts is arguable, and a late DoD payment is not clearly covered. Restoring the obligation in time avoids an Event of Default. Remedies need Required Lenders to act.

slides.label: Cash tests

exhibit.title: If Defense payments are suspended, MP's liquidity depends on two cash tests: $500m at each quarter-end and $343.75m on day 60
exhibit.subtitle: USD million at 30 September 2026; contractual thresholds beside reported balances
exhibit.annotation: Each threshold applies on its own date. Cash can be spent between quarter-ends, so the projected quarter-end balance sets the spending limit. Every draw also repeats the representation that no material adverse effect has occurred.

Measured each quarter-end until the covenant trigger; a shortfall is an immediate Event of Default, with no equity cure found.
125% of the $275m commitments; certified on day 60, it adds 30 days of grace after a suspension or release.
Lenders may require cash collateral for these after an Event of Default.

slides.table_reason: Reported balances and contractual thresholds are unlike measures; rows with their rules avoid implying a subtraction.

exhibit.title: Leverage tests start by Q3 2027, before expected 2028 10X commissioning, and the 2030 notes can pull maturity into 2029
exhibit.subtitle: Reported dates, contract deadlines and one conditional date
exhibit.annotation: The trigger comes earlier at $400m of covenant EBITDA, later only on a late filing. On $1,043.1m of debt, 4.00x leverage needs about $232m of covenant EBITDA ($209m with 100% netting); 3.00x coverage, at most $108–109m. With enough 2030 notes left, maturity springs unless cash plus availability tops $1,078.5m or leverage is 2.00x or less.
exhibit.source: Credit agreement §§1.01, 6.01(b), 7.11; Q3 2026 10-Q, Note 8 and MD&A

exhibit.title: The Defense agreements that support MP are also revolver default triggers
exhibit.subtitle: Government instruments linked to MP Materials; the transaction, offtake and price protection agreements are named in the credit agreement
exhibit.annotation: The price floor and offtake reduce MP's NdPr price and magnet volume risk; MP keeps 10X cost and timing risk. DoD can suspend offtake only after an uncured MP payment default; the price agreement has no suspension right. An uncured 10X breach is likelier: it makes the agreement terminable, an immediate revolver Event of Default.
exhibit.source: Transaction agreement §§6.13, 9.02(a); offtake §8.4; price protection §8(p)–(q); credit agreement §8.01(m); 2025 10-K, Note 3

data.relationship: Declared government links; spokes carry no value.

slides.label: Criteria

exhibit.title: Equity plus a revolver adds later liquidity but exposes MP to lender remedies if Defense payments are suspended
exhibit.subtitle: Four financing paths against seven criteria; marks are categorical and unweighted
exhibit.annotation: Analyst judgment. Equity plus revolver and equity only differ on four criteria: covenants, conditional liquidity, lender remedies and refinancing. Marks for committed debt rest on the commitment alone; "Not stated" means its loan terms were never published.
exhibit.source: FI003 analysis; credit agreement; prospectus supplement; 2025 10-K

criteria.label: Capital raised or committed before build
Avoids lender remedies if DoD suspends

slides.table_reason: Four options against seven categorical criteria need a matrix; a chart would imply a numeric scale the marks do not have.

exhibit.title: A minimum-payment addback in covenant earnings can reverse when cash arrives
exhibit.subtitle: Illustrative clause arithmetic with hypothetical inputs, not reported MP results
exhibit.annotation: Where the minimum payment exceeds attributable income, covenant EBITDA adds back the difference (20 on hypothetical 40 and 20). Cash later received for the same amount reverses it, so it counts once. The text leaves open whether the addback applies during a suspension. Covenant EBITDA differs from Adjusted EBITDA.
exhibit.source: Credit agreement, definition of Consolidated EBITDA

nodes.label: Does later cash repeat the addback?

slides.label: Strongest alternative

exhibit.title: The revolver helps in a fundable overrun; a suspension of Defense payments blocks it
exhibit.subtitle: Equity plus revolver against equity only, each with $724.2m of equity at the same dilution, in five situations
exhibit.annotation: Analyst judgment. Before the covenant trigger, a draw adds cash toward the $500m quarter-end test; after it, a draw raises leverage against the 4.00x limit. Equity only is better if covenant EBITDA would fall short of about $232m at the first leverage test.
exhibit.source: FI003 analysis; credit agreement; transaction agreement §9.02(a); 2025 10-K; Q3 2026 10-Q

exhibit.title: Equity first needs an open equity window, cash to finish 10X, secure Defense payments and covenant EBITDA near $232m
exhibit.subtitle: Decision conditions for a hypothetical sponsor; the highlighted route ends at the recommendation
exhibit.annotation: Analyst judgment. Set go and slow decisions on 10X against projected quarter-end cash of at least $500m, then covenant EBITDA of at least about $232m ($209m on the 100% reading). Revolver capacity is a secondary buffer. A sponsor without an anchor offtake or price floor may find the equity window closed.
exhibit.source: FI003 analysis; credit agreement; transaction agreement
